title: Largest government debts, in US dollars
hook: Which country's government owes the most money?

source.name: IMF DataMapper API — General government gross debt (Percent of GDP) x GDP, current prices (Billions of U.S. dollars); World Economic Outlook (April 2026)
source.terms: IMF data, free to use with attribution under the IMF Copyright and Usage terms (https://www.imf.org/en/About/copyright-and-terms); cite 'IMF, World Economic Outlook'.
source.notes: debt_usd_bn = GGXWDG_NGDP/100 x NGDPD, computed per country-year; both series last modified 2026-04-08 16:07:44 / 2026-04-08 16:07:35. Cut at 2024: the WEO carries 2025+ as estimates/projections. The DataMapper API does not expose each country's 'estimates start after' year, so some 2024 (and, for late-reporting countries, earlier) values may be IMF staff estimates. Debt-ratio coverage starts late for several large economies, so the early years under-count: first year with data — New Zealand 1985, Italy 1988, Austria 1988, Australia 1989, Switzerland 1990, Germany 1991, India 1991, China, People's Republic of 1995, Mexico 1996, Russian Federation 1997, Brazil 2000, United States 2001. Every one of the 2024 top 10 has data from 2001; a race that should read as complete must start at recommendedStart (2001). No gaps inside any entity's run. Countries only: 32 DataMapper keys dropped as regions/groups (ADVEC, AFQ, SSQ, AS5, APQ, AZQ, CBQ, CMQ, CAQ, EAQ, EEQ, DA, EDE, OEMDC, EURO, EUQ, EU, WE, MAE, MEQ, MECA, NAQ, NMQ, OAE, PIQ, SMQ, SAQ, SEQ, SSA, WEQ, WHQ, WEOWORLD). Entities are the economies in the IMF 'countries' list, named as the IMF labels them.
